title: What text blocks changed, and what they did not

questions.stem: Per this page, how does a text block compare at run time with a traditional literal holding the same characters?

options.text: The text block is slower, since its indentation is removed each time the line runs
options.says: The page says the compiler removes the indentation, so nothing is left to do when the line runs.

options.text: The text block is faster, since its lines are kept apart until they are printed
options.says: The page says the class file holds one plain String constant, not separate lines.

options.text: There is no difference, since both become the same interned string constant
options.says: The page says both compile to one plain String constant in the pool, so equals and even == return true.

questions.stem: Per this page, in which release did text blocks stop being a preview feature?

options.says: The page lists JEP 378 in Java 15 as the release that made text blocks standard.
The page lists JEP 368 in Java 14 as the second preview, the one that added the two new escapes.
The page lists JEP 355 in Java 13 as the first preview of text blocks.
